title: Analyzing Failure Modes in Semantic Role Labeling (SRL)
text:
The primary vulnerability of Semantic Role Labeling occurs when the system struggles with argument structure in highly complex or abstractly defined linguistic environments. One critical failure mode is inadequate handling of discourse phenomena, such as presupposition or coreference resolution, which requires understanding roles across multiple sentences rather than locally within a single clause.

Furthermore, SRL models frequently break down when confronted with implicit arguments or extremely long-distance dependencies. For instance, if the agent performing an action (the Arg0 role) is mentioned early in a paragraph and not explicitly attached to the target predicate using proximate syntactic markers, the system may fail to correctly link the semantic relationship. These challenges highlight that successful SRL relies not merely on robust dependency parsing but requires deep common-sense knowledge to bridge contextual gaps.
